newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Stals says may need to tighten monetary policy.
newsitem.headline: Stals says may need to tighten monetary policy.

text.p: South African Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said on Friday that the central bank might need to tighten monetary policy if there was no sign of a slowdown in bank credit extension and money supply growth.
"The latest available information begs the question whether monetary policy in its present form is restrictive enough," Stals told a conference.
The Reserve Bank was eagerly awaiting confirmation of a slowdown in monetary aggregates, but Stals hinted that September data due out at 1500 GMT would not show any dramatic decline.
The rate of increase in M3 money supply had remained above 15 percent throughout the first nine months of 1996, he said.
Economists polled by Reuters had forecast a marginal slowdown in M3 growth last month to 15.1 percent year-on-year from 15.5 percent in August.
Stals said there was evidence that M3 and credit extension had started to level out at relatively high rates of increase, but the central bank was growing impatient for signs of an actual decline.
"Up to now, the monetary authorities were prepared to be tolerant, and to wait for further signals of an actual decline in the growth rates of these important anchors for monetary policy," he said.
"Should new statistics contradict this assumption, there will be no alternative but to tighten monetary policy further."
Commenting on the balance of payments, Stals said there were some signs that the current account deficit was starting to narrow.

This was supported by an apparent slowdown in gross domestic expenditure, the fall in the rand which had made imports more expensive and boosted exports, and the increasing effect of tight domestic financial conditions.
